topic: What is the Model Context Protocol (MCP)?
expected_points: MCP is an open standard for connecting AI applications to external tools and data sources
It uses a client/server design where servers expose tools a model can call
It was created by Anthropic

topic: How does retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) work?
expected_points: Relevant documents are retrieved from a store, usually by embedding similarity
The retrieved text is added to the prompt before the model generates its answer
Grounding answers in retrieved sources reduces hallucination

topic: What is LangGraph and how does it differ from LangChain?
expected_points: LangGraph models an agent workflow as a graph of nodes sharing state
It supports loops, persistence and pausing for human input
It targets stateful, long-running workflows rather than simple linear chains

topic: Why did DRAM prices rise sharply in 2026?
expected_points: Demand from AI and data centres pulled manufacturing capacity away from consumer memory
Manufacturers prioritised higher-margin products, constraining supply
Consumer memory prices rose sharply as a result

topic: What are vector databases used for?
expected_points: They store vector embeddings of text or other data
They find similar items by nearest-neighbour search rather than exact matching
They are commonly used for semantic search and RAG

topic: What is quantization in large language models?
expected_points: Model weights are stored at lower numeric precision than the original format
This cuts memory use and can speed up inference
Some accuracy is traded away for the efficiency gain

topic: How does Ollama run large language models locally?
expected_points: Ollama runs language models on your own machine instead of in the cloud
Models are downloaded and stored locally, then served through a local API
Because inference happens locally, your data stays on the machine

topic: What is OAuth 2.0 and how does the authorization code flow work?
expected_points: The user is redirected to an authorization server to approve access
The client receives a short-lived authorization code and exchanges it for an access token
The client calls the API with that token rather than the user's password

topic: What are the trade-offs of multi-agent versus single-agent LLM systems?
expected_points: Splitting work across specialised agents lets each focus on one job
Coordinating them adds complexity, latency and cost
A single agent is simpler but harder to steer over a long task

topic: How does PostgreSQL implement MVCC?
expected_points: Each transaction sees a snapshot of the data, with multiple row versions kept
Readers and writers do not block each other
Obsolete row versions have to be cleaned up afterwards

topic: What is LLM-as-a-judge evaluation?
expected_points: A model scores or compares outputs against a rubric instead of exact string matching
It suits open-ended tasks where there is no single correct answer
Judges can be biased or inconsistent, so the scores need care

topic: What does a checkpointer do in a stateful agent workflow?
expected_points: It saves the workflow's state as the run progresses
A saved run can be resumed later, including after pausing for human input
State is stored per run so separate runs do not mix

topic: What is the difference between fine-tuning and prompt engineering?
expected_points: Fine-tuning changes the model's weights by training it on task data
Prompt engineering changes only the input and leaves the model unchanged
Fine-tuning costs more and needs data, while prompting is faster to iterate on

topic: How do WebSockets differ from HTTP long polling?
expected_points: WebSockets keep one connection open for two-way messaging after an HTTP upgrade
Long polling repeatedly issues requests that the server holds until it has data
WebSockets have lower latency and less overhead for frequent updates
